name: M01 revealed server seed corrupted mid-phase
guard: Step 1 hashes every revealed server seed to the preceding epoch's published commitment; a revealed seed that does not hash to its commitment is the failure commit-reveal exists to detect.

name: M02 forward commitment link broken
guard: Step 2 requires seeds[i].nextServerSeedHash === seeds[i+1].serverSeedHashed on every rotation, so the ORDER of the epochs is pre-committed.

name: M03 foreign commitment inside an epoch
guard: Step 3 keys epochs by the capture timeline, not by the hash under test, so a bet carrying another epoch's hash inside a window is a disagreement with the rotation record. The old form grouped by the hash itself and could not fail.
replace:
bets[10].seed.serverSeedHashed = bets[60].seed.serverSeedHashed; // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M04 nonce repeated inside an epoch
guard: Step 4 requires each epoch to run 0..49 from the DECLARED base; a repeat that is not the single capture-retry pattern is operator-side — HARD FAIL, not a capture-origin FLAG.

name: M04b nonces reordered with no gap
guard: Swapping two nonces leaves the SORTED sequence 0..49 intact, so only the capture-order check (strictly increasing in the order recorded, before any sort) can see it.
replace:
[bets[5].seed.nonce, bets[6].seed.nonce] = [bets[6].seed.nonce, bets[5].seed.nonce]; // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M05 drawn set altered on a captured bet
guard: Step 5 recomputes every draw from (serverSeed, clientSeed, nonce); a served draw the algorithm does not produce is the core failure mode.

name: M05b one epoch's revealed seed dropped
guard: With a revealed seed missing, 50 bets cannot be recomputed and there are ZERO mismatches; only the coverage bound (recomputed == EXPECTED_BETS) catches it.

name: M05c served draw padded with a duplicate
guard: A served drawn_numbers padded with a repeat of its own first number has the SAME Set as the true draw, so the set comparison passes; only the served-structure assertion (exactly 10 distinct numbers in 1-40) catches it (KENO-10).
replace:
bets[0].response.drawn_numbers = [...bets[0].response.drawn_numbers, bets[0].response.drawn_numbers[0]]; // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M05d duplicate pick in a pick set
guard: A pick set with a repeated number is not a legal Keno bet; Step 5 asserts pick legality (size, distinctness, range, request.picks) on every bet (KENO-10).
replace:
bets[0].request.selected_positions = [bets[0].request.selected_positions[0], ...bets[0].request.selected_positions.slice(0, -1)]; bets[0].response.selected_positions = bets[0].request.selected_positions; // MUTATION: same size, first pick duplicated
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M05e pick independence no longer witnessed on data
expect: no epoch carries more than one pick set
guard: KENO-17 requires the pick-free derivation to be witnessed across bets that share a seed pair and differ in their picks. Giving every bet its epoch's first pick set removes the witness; Step 5 must say the property is no longer shown rather than pass on the argument count alone.
replace:
for (const b of bets) { const f = bets.find(x => x.seed.serverSeedHashed === b.seed.serverSeedHashed)!; b.request.selected_positions = [...f.request.selected_positions]; b.response.selected_positions = [...f.request.selected_positions]; b.request.picks = f.request.picks; } // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M06 draw ignores the client seed
guard: If the HMAC message drops the client seed, a wrong client seed reproduces every draw; Step 6 requires every draw to change.

name: M06b empty-seed control neutered
guard: Step 6's empty-seed control recomputes every bet with clientSeed = ''. Making the 'empty' draw use the REAL client seed makes all 5,100 collide; only the empty-seed half can see it (the wrong-seed half is untouched).
replace: const emptyDraw   = computeDrawFromBuffer(key, bet.seed.clientSeed, bet.seed.nonce); // MUTATION

name: M07 a win nudged by one 1e-16 unit
guard: Step 7 compares amount_won with amount x round13(recomputed cell) on integers. A credit moved by 1e-16 — which the former relative 1e-12 on doubles forgave — must FAIL.
replace:
{ const w = bets.find(b => b.response.amount_won !== '0')!; const s = w.response.amount_won; w.response.amount_won = s.padEnd(s.indexOf('.') + 17, '0').replace(/0$/, '1'); } // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M07b forged win in a re-pinned dataset
guard: Forged evidence: the dataset is edited AND its SHA-256 pin re-pinned, so the pre-flight abort and Step 14 both accept it; the payout recomputation must still reject the forged credit.

name: M08 served multiplier nudged by one 13-dp unit
guard: Step 7 settles from the RECOMPUTED cell, so a doctored served multiplier with an untouched amount_won passes Step 7; Step 8 compares the served string with the display-rounded cell exactly.
replace:
{ const w = bets.find(b => b.response.multiplier === '1.1')!; w.response.multiplier = '1.1000000000001'; } // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M09 a Phase D bet relabelled
guard: Step 9 binds the elevated-stake population to the capture plan (100 Phase D bets at $10); a Phase D that is not the plan's did not show bet-size invariance.
replace:
bets.filter(b => b.phase === 'D')[0].request.amount = '9.99'; // MUTATION: an elevated-stake bet off the $10 stake
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M10 configuration floor above the leanest config
guard: Step 10 scores the per-config floor from src/loader.ts; raising it above the leanest config's 73 bets must FAIL, proving the floor is enforced rather than printed.

name: M11 a bet served a scaled edge
guard: Step 11 is the declarationTruth for KENO-31 n/a: every bet must be served the flat edge 0.1; a single scaled edge FAILs it.

name: M12 a new consolation cell in a re-pinned config
guard: Step 12 enumerates every non-monotone cell of the table and requires the declared list exactly; a table that grows a consolation payout on HIGH picks=1 (config re-pinned so the pre-flight accepts it) must FAIL.

name: M12b a payout cap key appears in the config
guard: Step 12 declares the cap UNDECLARED on the evidence that the pinned config carries no limit key; a config (re-pinned) that carries max_payout must FAIL, so the n/a is a reading of the config and not a constant.

name: M13 a phase label corrupted
guard: Step 13 counts bets per phase against src/loader.ts constants; a relabelled bet breaks the per-phase population.

name: M14 dataset altered and the pre-flight abort disabled
guard: With the pre-flight dataset abort off, Step 14's own SHA-256 comparison is what stands between a doctored dataset and a Full Pass.

name: M15 one bet removed from an epoch
guard: Step 15 pins every epoch to exactly 50 bets and the epoch count to 102.

name: M16 hit probability no longer hypergeometric
guard: Step 16 checks the picks=10 mode of the model every RTP rests on; replacing C(N-n, d-k) by C(N-n, k) moves the mode to 10.
find: return (comb(picks, hits) * comb(grid - picks, drawn - hits)) / comb(grid, drawn);
replace: return (comb(picks, hits) * comb(grid - picks, hits)) / comb(grid, drawn); // MUTATION

name: M17 an unreached table cell changed in a re-pinned config
guard: HIGH picks=10 hits=10 was never reached in live play (payout-coverage.json), so no served multiplier can contradict it; the analytic RTP identity — double and exact — must reject it on its own.

name: M17b table negative control neutered
guard: Step 17's table negative control bumps one cell by one unit in its last place and requires the exact RTP check to reject it. Leaving the cell unchanged makes the control vacuous; the step must catch its own defeated control.

name: M17c law negative control neutered
guard: Step 17's law negative control corrupts one weight by one unit and requires the exact identity check to reject it; corrupting by 0 makes it vacuous.

name: M18 Phase D client seeds collapsed to one
guard: Step 18 requires two distinct Phase D client seeds, one per Phase D epoch.
replace:
{ const d = bets.filter(b => b.phase === 'D'); for (const b of d) b.seed.clientSeed = d[0].seed.clientSeed; } // MUTATION
const byHash = groupByHash(bets);

name: M19 Pass 1 failure count forged
guard: Step 19 recounts chi2FailsAtAlpha01 from the shipped rows; a forged scalar disagrees with the recount.

name: M19b uniformity statistic forged
expect: uniformity statistic / p does not recompute
guard: Step 19 recomputes each row's without-replacement-corrected grid-uniformity X² from its shipped per-number counts (KENO-20); a forged statistic disagrees.

name: M19d serial sufficient statistic forged
expect: do not re-derive from the shipped integers
guard: Step 19 re-derives r1 exactly from the hit histogram and the shipped Σ x_t·x_{t+1}; a forged pair sum moves the exact r1 far beyond the 1e-9 bound (KENO-20).

name: M19c Pass 1 replay seed altered
guard: Step 19 replays the first 1,000 rounds of every config from the pinned seed pairs and requires the artifact's 1K convergence point bit for bit; a seed that is not the one the artifact came from must FAIL (KENO-20 replay).

name: M19e one Pass 1 runs-test p forged just beyond the reproduction bound
expect: do not re-derive from the shipped integers
guard: Step 19 compares each recomputed runs p (normalCDF, libm) and grid-uniformity p (incomplete gamma) to the shipped value at 1e-14 absolute + 1e-12 relative (src/diff.ts numbersAgree), not bit equality, so 1-ulp libm drift across platforms passes; a shipped runsPValue moved by 1e-12 (bound 7.1e-13 at p = 0.700) must still FAIL. The row's serial flag is unchanged, so only the recomputation can catch it.

name: M20 Pass 2 cherry-pick flag count forged
guard: Step 20 recounts test_b_cherry_pick_flags from the rows' own p-values; a forged header disagrees.

name: M20b early-window histogram forged
guard: Step 20 recomputes every row's chi² / p from its shipped histograms and checks full = early + late (KENO-21); moving one early count breaks both.

name: M20c early window replayed one nonce off
guard: Step 20 replays every Pass 2 row's early window (nonces 0–49) from the revealed seed and requires the shipped histogram; replaying nonces 1–50 must FAIL (KENO-21, every window re-derived).
find: for (let nonce = 0; nonce < EW; nonce++) draws.push(computeDrawFromBuffer(key, cs, nonce,
replace: for (let nonce = 0; nonce < EW; nonce++) draws.push(computeDrawFromBuffer(key, cs, nonce + 1,

name: M20d served return collapsed to zero hits
guard: The pre-registered return statistic must be able to fail: if every served bet paid its zero-hit cell, the return of the captured window sits far below its exact null and the bootstrap lower-tail p is < 0.01 (KENO-21).

name: M20e one Pass 2 p-value forged just beyond the reproduction bound
expect: chi² / p does not recompute from its shipped histograms
guard: Step 20 compares each recomputed chi² / p to the shipped value at 1e-14 absolute + 1e-12 relative (the reproduction rule), not bit equality, so 1-ulp libm drift across platforms passes; a shipped p moved by 1e-12 (bound 8.3e-13 at p = 0.816) must still FAIL. The flag outcome of the row is unchanged, so only the recomputation can catch it.

name: M21 pinned artifact bytes changed with every value intact
guard: Whitespace-only change to determinism-log.json: every value is intact so the field-level reproduction gate cannot see it; only the byte pin can.

name: M21b impossible value in a re-pinned artifact
guard: Forged evidence: determinism-log.json claims -1 mismatches AND is re-pinned in src/artifact-pins.ts, so the byte pin accepts it; only the value-domain check (bounds from src/domains.ts, never from the artifact) can reject a negative count.

name: M22 rejection ceiling removed (naive modulo)
guard: With maxFair = 2^32 (every chunk accepted) the draw is a naive modulo: its bias (1.397e-10 at range 40) sits UNDER the 2^-32 floor and a value >= 0xFFFFFFF0 is so rare that all 5,100 draws still recompute; only Step 22's exactness enumeration can see it.

name: M22b rejection census under-counted
guard: The census is bound to 39 x 5,100 accepted chunks; a draw that stops counting scanned chunks breaks the binding.

name: M23 vendored docs-site derive.js edited
guard: The vendored docs-site verifier must hash to its pin before it is executed.

name: M23b vendored live-site chunk edited
guard: The vendored live-site bundle must hash to its pins before the runner executes it.

name: M23c docs-site derive draws a different set and is re-pinned
expect: docs-site verifier drew a different set
guard: Forged evidence: the vendored derive.js is changed to return positions 1..10 instead of 0..9 AND its pin re-pinned, so the hash check accepts it; executing it on every bet must still expose the different draw.

name: M23d docs-site paytable cell changed and re-pinned
guard: Forged evidence: one cell of the vendored docs-site paytables.js (HIGH picks=1 hits=1) is changed AND re-pinned, so the hash check accepts it; Step 23 compares the site table with the pinned kenoConfig.json cell for cell and the printed multiplier with the served one on every bet, so it must FAIL (the defect found on the stale repotree-sync build, PV-1).

name: M23e operator Verify-tab file logic changed and re-pinned
guard: Forged evidence: Duel's own vendored Keno Verify-tab code is changed (the shuffle's first cursor starts one step late) AND its SHA-256 pin re-computed, so the hash check accepts it; executing it on every bet and comparing with src/rng.ts and the served draw must expose it (KENO-09).

name: M23f operator Verify-tab file byte changed without re-pin
expect: operator Verify-tab code or its runner does not match its pinned SHA-256
guard: The vendored operator file must hash to its pin before it runs (KENO-09).

name: M23g src/rng.ts returns the drawn numbers out of shuffle order
expect: operator Verify-tab code disagrees: in order with src/rng.ts
guard: The served drawn_numbers are compared as a set (their order is not the shuffle order, spec O1), so a draw returned in the wrong order still reproduces every served set; only the in-order comparison with Duel's Verify-tab code, run as a second check (KENO-09), sees it.
